question: A 24-year-old, gravida 1, para 1 woman develops lower abdominal pain and fevers 4 days after undergoing a cesarean delivery under general anesthesia for prolonged labor. Since delivery, she has had malodorous lochia and difficulty breastfeeding due to breast pain. She has not had any shortness of breath or chest pain. She received intravenous intrapartum penicillin for group B streptococcus prophylaxis, but does not take any other medications on a regular basis. She appears ill. Her temperature is 38.8°C (102°F), pulse is 120/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows a urinary catheter in place. Breasts are engorged and tender. Nipples are cracked with mild erythema. There is erythema surrounding a mildly tender, dry, low transverse, 12-cm incision in the lower abdomen. Pelvic examination shows dark-red, foul-smelling lochia and uterine tenderness. Her hemoglobin concentration is 9 g/dL, leukocyte count is 16,000/mm3, and platelet count is 300,000/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's fever?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cesarean delivery -> postpartum period -> fever -> 60% CHAIN: Cesarean delivery -> prolonged labor -> increased risk of infection -> 70% CHAIN: Cesarean delivery -> general anesthesia -> impaired immune response -> increased risk of infection -> 80% CHAIN: Cesarean delivery -> intrapartum penicillin -> group B streptococcus prophylaxis -> potential antibiotic-resistant infection -> 70% CHAIN: Lower abdominal pain -> erythema surrounding incision -> possible wound infection -> 80% CHAIN: Malodorous lochia -> uterine tenderness -> possible endometritis -> 90% CHAIN: Breast pain -> engorged and tender breasts -> cracked nipples with erythema -> possible mastitis -> 70% CHAIN: Fever -> postpartum period -> endometritis -> 60%
analysis: The patient presents with fever, lower abdominal pain, foul-smelling lochia, breast engorgement, and uterine tenderness, which are all suggestive of an infection. Given the timing post-cesarean delivery and the clinical findings, the most likely cause of her fever is endometritis, which is an infection of the uterine lining.
